# Fixing a Vatti-style Polygon Clipping Engine for Self-Intersecting Contours and Coincident Edges

## Root-cause analysis

A Vatti-family sweep walks a scanbeam and flips fill parity at each boundary crossing. For a **coincident (shared) edge** the beam crosses two boundary edges at the same `x`, so parity flips twice and must cancel. Four concrete defects caused the reported failures:

1. **Clearance probe jumps the nearest parallel boundary.** The inside/outside probe is offset along a sub-edge normal, and the offset must stay smaller than the distance to the nearest other edge. The original code skipped *all parallel* edges (to avoid coincident ones) — but a nearby **parallel-but-distinct** edge (thin band from a self-intersection) constrains the probe. Skipping it overshoots → wrong classification → unbalanced directed-edge graph → open/spurious output rings.
2. **Hole touching its outer yields a figure-eight.** At the touching vertex four boundary half-edges meet. The angular "region-on-the-left" join correctly walks the region boundary, but a disk-with-a-touching-hole has a *single self-touching* closed boundary → a ring that **revisits a vertex**.
3. **Dropped holes.** Hole→outer assignment used a hole **vertex** as representative; when the hole touches its outer that vertex lies on the outer boundary, where point-in-polygon is undefined, so the hole was discarded.
4. Collinear/duplicate vertices left on output made results noisy.

## The fix

Split every edge at every intersection/touch first (with a snapping point registry so coincident coordinates share one point id), then classify each sub-edge by the *result region it borders* — this makes the "flip twice" pair either both non-boundary or the same deduplicated directed edge.

Key routines (full engine in `vatti-clip.js` / embedded in `SOLUTION.md`):

```javascript
// Defect 1: only *coincident* same-line edges are ignored; parallel-but-distinct
// edges constrain the offset by their perpendicular separation.
const cross = ux * ey - uy * ex;
if (Math.abs(cross) < 1e-12 * clen) {
  const off = Math.abs(ux * (c.y - a.y) - uy * (c.x - a.x)); // perp separation
  const scale = Math.max(1, Math.abs(c.x), Math.abs(c.y), Math.abs(a.x), Math.abs(a.y));
  if (off > 1e-9 * scale && off < best) best = off;   // distinct parallel line: constrains
  continue;                                           // same line (coincident): ignore
}
const dd = Math.sqrt(dist2PointSeg(mx, my, c, d));
if (dd < best) best = dd;
let delta = Math.min(len / 4, (isFinite(best) ? best : len) / 4);

// Defect 2: split a self-touching closed walk into simple loops at repeated vertices.
const splitWalk = (verts) => { /* stack + pos-map; pop loop on repeat */ };

// Defect 3: representative point strictly inside the hole.
const interiorPoint = (ring) => { /* centroid, else offset an edge midpoint inward */ };
```

Then group holes into the smallest containing outer using `interiorPoint`, and strip collinear/duplicate vertices.

## Verification

Anchored to the **predicate** (membership of the output must equal `A∧B`, `A∧¬B`, `A∨B`, `A⊕B` sampled off all edges), not to another library — because `polygon-clipping@0.15.7` itself drops a whole region on one of these degenerate inputs.

```
$ node vatti-clip.test.js
13 passed, 0 failed

$ node vatti-clip.selftest.js grid 3000 6      # tiny integer grid → many coincident edges
all 3000 grid cases OK (1452000 membership checks)

$ node vatti-clip.selftest.js real 2000 20     # fractional coordinates
all 2000 real cases OK (12168000 membership checks)
```

The explicit suite pins the named degeneracies: identical `difference` → `[]` (coincident edges cancel), shared-edge `union` → merged rectangle with no internal edge, bow-tie → both lobes, and a hole touching its outer → separate CW hole ring rather than a self-touching contour.

The complete, directly usable markdown (with the entire engine source embedded) is at `~/SOLUTION.md`; the runnable engine is `~/vatti-clip.js`.

signatures.description: Implement a Vatti-style polygon clipping engine that executes a boolean operation (intersection or difference) between two polygons whose contours may be self-intersecting and share coincident edges. The algorithm must find all pairwise edge intersections, split edges at intersection points, build a Double-Ended Queue classification of local minima/maxima, and join output contours while correctly handling the degenerate shared-edge case where scanbeam parity flips twice at the same x. Common failure: output contours that revisit a vertex or drop holes when coincident edges cancel.
